---
title: "Flat Morphisms"
subtitle: ""
description: "Flat modules and morphisms, practical criteria for flatness, and their role in smooth and étale geometry."
order: 50
---

Here we study the properties of flat morphisms that we will need as background for étale morphisms.

## Flatness

::: {#def-flat-sheaf name="flat quasi-coherent sheaf over a base"}
Let $\pi\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and let $\mathcal F$ be a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. We say that $\mathcal F$ is **flat over
$Y$ at $x\in X$** if the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is flat as an
$\mathcal O_{Y,\pi(x)}$-module. It is **flat over $Y$** if this holds at every
point of $X$.
:::

On affine opens, this reduces to the familiar algebraic notion: if
$X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$, and
$\mathcal F=\widetilde M$, then flatness is controlled by the $B$-module $M$ coming from $B\to A$.

::: {#lem-flat-is-local name=""}
With the notation above, $\mathcal F$ is flat over $Y$ if and only if $M$ is flat as a $B$-module.
:::

:::{.proof}
It is an easy commutative algebra exercise.
:::

::: {#cor-pushforward-flat-sheaf name=""}
If $\pi:X\to Y$ is an affine morphism, and $\mathcal F$ is a quasicoherent sheaf on $X$, then $\mathcal F$ is flat over $Y$ if and only if $\pi_*\mathcal F$ is flat over $Y$.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="nonexample"}
The statement may fail even when $\pi$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

Consider the composite
$$
\pi\colon \mathbb P^1_k\hookrightarrow \mathbb P^1_{k[x]} \to \operatorname{Spec}k[x],
\text{ and set }
\mathcal F=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1_k}(-1).
$$
Then $\mathcal F$ is a line bundle and hence flat over $\mathbb P^1_{k}$.

On the other hand, the global section of $\pi_*\mathcal F$ is $H^0(\mathbf P^1_k,\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}(-1))=0$, which implies that $\pi_*\mathcal F$ is not flat.
:::

::: {#def-flat-morphism name="flat morphism"}
A morphism $\pi\colon X\to Y$ is **flat at $x\in X$** if the local ring
$\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,\pi(x)}$. It is **flat** if it
is flat at every point, i.e. $\mathcal O_X$ is flat over $Y$.

Equivalently, by @lem-flat-is-local, $\pi\colon X\to Y$ is flat if there exist affine open coverings $X=\bigcup_i X_i$ and $Y=\bigcup_i Y_i$ such that $\pi(X_i)\subseteq Y_i$ for each $i$, and $A_i$ is flat over $B_i$ whenever $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$.
:::

::: {#prp-flat-morphisms-reasonable name="flat morphisms form a reasonable class"}
Flat morphisms satisfy the following properties one expects from a geometric
class of morphisms:

1. isomorphisms and open immersions are flat;
2. the composite $\phi\circ\pi\colon X\to Z$ is flat whenever both $\pi$ and
   $\phi$ are flat;
3. flatness is preserved by base change: if $\pi\colon X\to Y$ is flat and
   $\psi\colon Y'\to Y$ is any morphism, then
   $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ is flat;
4. flatness is local on both the source and the target.
:::

::: {.proof}
The assersions 1 and 4 follow immediately by the definition. Assersion 2,3 follow from the corresponding properties for flat quasicoherent sheaves, see @lem-composite and @lem-base-change.
:::

::: {#lem-composite name=""}
Let $\pi\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism, and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasicoherent sheaf on $X$ that is flat over $Y$. Let $\phi\colon Y\to Z$ be a flat morphism. Then $\mathcal F$ is flat over $Z$.
:::

:::{.proof}
By definition, it suffices to check on stalks.
:::

::: {#lem-base-change name=""}
Let $X\to Y$ and $Y'\to Y$ be morphisms. Let $\mu\colon X'=X\times_Y Y'\to X$ be the projection, and $\mathcal F$ a quasicoherent sheaf on $X$ flat over $Y$. Then $\mu^*\mathcal F$ is flat over $Y'$.
:::

:::{.proof}
By definition, it suffices to check on stalks. Let $x'\in X'$. Assume that $x'$ maps to $x\in X$, $y'\in Y'$ and $y\in Y$ respectively. Then $\mathcal O_{X',x'}\cong (\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}} \mathcal O_{Y',y'})_{\mathfrak p}$ for some prime ideal $\mathfrak p$. Then 
$$
(\mu^*\mathcal F)_{x'}\cong (\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}} \mathcal O_{Y',y'})_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal F_x.
$$
The rest is a commutative algebra exercise.
:::

::: {prp-flat-exact name=""}
Let $\pi:X\to Y$ be a flat morphism, then the pullback 
$$
\pi^*:\operatorname{Qcoh}_Y\to\operatorname{Qcoh}_X
$$ 
is an exact functor.
:::

## Criteria of flatness

::: {#prp-tor-criterion name="Tor criterion"}
A $B$-module $M$ is flat if and only if

$$
\operatorname{Tor}_1^B(M,N)=0
$$

for every $B$-module $N$.
:::

::: {#prp-ideal-criterion name="ideal criterion"}
A $B$-module $M$ is flat if and only if, for every finitely generated ideal
$I\subseteq B$, the natural map

$$
I\otimes_B M\longrightarrow M
$$

is injective. The map sends $a\otimes m$ to $am$. Equivalently, we can only check $N$ for finitely generated ideals of $B$ in @prp-tor-criterion.
:::

::: {#prp-local-rings name=""}
Let $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finitely generated $B$-module. If $\operatorname{Tor}(M,B/\mathfrak n)=0$, then $M$ is free.
:::

::: {#prp-local-criterion name="local criterion"}
Let $(B,\mathfrak n)\to (A,\mathfrak m)$ be a local morphism of Noetherian local rings, and $M$ a finitely generated $A$ module. Then $M$ is $B$-flat if and only if $\operatorname {Tor}^B_1(M,B/\mathfrak n)=0$.
:::

::: {#prp-slicing-flatness-target name="slicing criterion for flatness on the target"}
Let $(B,\mathfrak n)\to (A,\mathfrak m)$ be a local morphism of Noetherian local rings, $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module, and $t\in \mathfrak n$ a non-zerodivisor on $B$. Then $M$ is flat over $B$ if and only if

1. $t$ is not a zerodivisor on $M$, and
2. $M/tM$ is flat over $B/(t)$.
:::

::: {#prp-slicing-flatness-source name=""}
Suppose $(B,\mathfrak n)\to(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a local morphism of Noetherian local rings, $M$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, and $t\in\mathfrak m\subset A$ is a non-zerodivisor on $M/\mathfrak nM$. If $M$ is flat over $B$, then $M/tM$ is flat over $B$
:::


### Closed immersion is well-behaved under the condition of flatness

::: {#prp-pullback-qcoh name="Pullback of quasicoherent sheaves"}
Let $0 \to \mathscr{F}' \to \mathscr{F} \to \mathscr{F}'' \to 0$ be a short exact sequence of quasicoherent sheaves on a scheme $Y$, and $\mathscr{F}''$ is flat. Let $\pi\colon X \to Y$ be any morphism of schemes. Then the pulled back sequence $0 \to \pi^*\mathscr{F}' \to \pi^*\mathscr{F} \to \pi^*\mathscr{F}'' \to 0$ remains exact.
:::

::: {#prp-flat-ideal-sheaf name=""}
Let $f\colon X\to Z$ and $\beta\colon Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes, and let $i\colon V\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion. Set
$$
W=X\times_ZY,\qquad V_Y=V\times_ZY,
$$
and denote the induced morphisms by $\alpha\colon W\to X$ and $i'\colon V_Y\hookrightarrow W$. If either $\beta$ or the composite $V\to X\to Z$ is flat, then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\alpha^*\mathcal I_{V/X}\cong\mathcal I_{V_Y/W}.
$$
Equivalently, the pullback of the ideal sequence of $V$ remains exact:
$$
0\longrightarrow\alpha^*\mathcal I_{V/X}
\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W
\longrightarrow i'_*\mathcal O_{V_Y}
\longrightarrow0.
$$

::: {.proof}
 Since $i$ is affine, affine base change gives a canonical isomorphism
$$
\alpha^*i_*\mathcal O_V\cong i'_*\mathcal O_{V_Y}.
$$
The ideal sequence of the closed immersion $i$ is
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal I_{V/X}
\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X
\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_V
\longrightarrow0.
$$
If $\beta$ is flat, then its base change $\alpha$ is flat. Hence $\alpha^*$ is exact, so pulling back the ideal sequence gives
$$
0\longrightarrow\alpha^*\mathcal I_{V/X}
\longrightarrow\alpha^*\mathcal O_X
\longrightarrow\alpha^*i_*\mathcal O_V
\longrightarrow0.
$$
Using $\alpha^*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_W$ and the affine base-change isomorphism above, this becomes the asserted exact sequence.
Now suppose instead that $V\to Z$ is flat. Then $i_*\mathcal O_V$ is flat over $Z$. By @prp-pullback-qcoh, we still have the exact sequence we desire.
:::

## Flatness and Smoothness
We will show that smooth morphisms are flat. 

::: {#prp-smooth-is-flat name=""}
Every smooth morphism of schemes is flat.
:::

::: {.proof}
We first treat the case in which the schemes are locally Noetherian. Let $\pi\colon X\to Y$ be smooth, let $p\in X$, and put $q=\pi(p)$. After replacing $X$ and $Y$ by suitable affine neighborhoods of $p$ and $q$, respectively, we may write $\pi$ in the form

$$
\operatorname{Spec}\!\left(
B[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+r}]/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)
\right)
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec}B,
$$

where the Jacobian matrix of $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ has rank $r$ at $p$. Set

$$
S=B[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+r}],
\qquad
A_k=S/(f_1,\ldots,f_k)
\quad (0\leq k\leq r),
$$

and let $p_k\in\operatorname{Spec}A_k$ be the image of $p$. We prove inductively that $(A_k)_{p_k}$ is flat over $B_q$.

For $k=0$, the ring $(A_0)_{p_0}=S_{p_0}$ is flat over $B_q$, since a polynomial algebra is flat over its coefficient ring and localization preserves flatness.

Suppose that $(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}$ is flat over $B_q$. Let $t$ denote the image of $f_k$ in $(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}$. Since $p$ lies on $V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, we have $t\in p_{k-1}(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}$. We claim that $t$ is a non-zerodivisor on the fiber

$$
C_k
=
(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}/q(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}
\cong
\left(
\kappa(q)[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+r}]/(f_1,\ldots,f_{k-1})
\right)_{\bar p}.
$$

The first $k$ rows of the Jacobian matrix have rank $k$ at $p$. Consequently, the morphism

$$
\operatorname{Spec}A_{k-1}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B
$$

is smooth at $p_{k-1}$, so $C_k$ is reduced.

Choose variables $x_{j_1},\ldots,x_{j_k}$ such that

$$
\Delta_k
=
\det\!\left(
\frac{\partial f_a}{\partial x_{j_b}}
\right)_{1\leq a,b\leq k}
$$

is a unit at $\bar p$. On the localized polynomial ring over $\kappa(q)$, define a derivation by

$$
D(h)
=
\det
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_{j_1}} & \cdots &
\dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_{j_k}}\\
\vdots & & \vdots\\
\dfrac{\partial f_{k-1}}{\partial x_{j_1}} & \cdots &
\dfrac{\partial f_{k-1}}{\partial x_{j_k}}\\
\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x_{j_1}} & \cdots &
\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x_{j_k}}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For $a<k$, two rows in the determinant defining $D(f_a)$ coincide, so $D(f_a)=0$. Thus $D$ descends to a derivation of $C_k$, and $D(t)=\Delta_k$ is a unit in $C_k$.

If $g t=0$ in $C_k$, then

$$
0=D(gt)=D(g)t+gD(t).
$$

Multiplying by $g$ and using $gt=0$ gives $g^2D(t)=0$. Since $D(t)$ is a unit, $g^2=0$; since $C_k$ is reduced, $g=0$. Hence $t$ is a non-zerodivisor on $C_k$.

We may therefore apply the slicing criterion for flatness on the source to the local morphism

$$
(B_q,qB_q)
\longrightarrow
\bigl((A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}},p_{k-1}(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}\bigr),
$$

with $M=(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}$. It follows that

$$
(A_k)_{p_k}
\cong
(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}/t(A_{k-1})_{p_{k-1}}
$$

is flat over $B_q$. Induction gives that $(A_r)_{p_r}=\mathcal O_{X,p}$ is flat over $B_q=\mathcal O_{Y,q}$. Thus $\pi$ is flat at $p$, proving the proposition in the locally Noetherian case.

We now remove the Noetherian hypothesis. Flatness is local on the source and target, so around any $p\in X$ we may choose a standard smooth presentation

$$
U
=
\operatorname{Spec}\!\left(
\bigl(B[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+r}]/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\bigr)_{\Delta}
\right)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Spec}B,
$$

where, after reordering the variables,

$$
\Delta
=
\det\!\left(
\frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}
\right)_{1\leq i,j\leq r}
$$

is invertible on $U$.

Only finitely many coefficients of $B$ occur in the polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_r$. Introduce an indeterminate $c^i_{a_1,\ldots,a_{n+r}}$ for each such coefficient and let

$$
P
=
\mathbb Z
\left[
c^i_{a_1,\ldots,a_{n+r}}
\right].
$$

Define universal polynomials

$$
g_i
=
\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_{n+r}}
c^i_{a_1,\ldots,a_{n+r}}
x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_{n+r}^{a_{n+r}}
\in P[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+r}],
$$

where each sum is finite, and put

$$
\Delta_0
=
\det\!\left(
\frac{\partial g_i}{\partial x_j}
\right)_{1\leq i,j\leq r}.
$$

The morphism

$$
U_0
=
\operatorname{Spec}\!\left(
\bigl(P[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+r}]/(g_1,\ldots,g_r)\bigr)_{\Delta_0}
\right)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Spec}P
$$

is smooth. Since $P$ is Noetherian, the first part of the proof shows that $U_0\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ is flat.

There is a ring homomorphism $P\to B$ sending each universal coefficient $c^i_{a_1,\ldots,a_{n+r}}$ to the corresponding coefficient of $f_i$. Under this homomorphism, $g_i$ maps to $f_i$ and $\Delta_0$ maps to $\Delta$. Hence

$$
U
\cong
U_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}P}\operatorname{Spec}B.
$$

Thus $\pi|_U$ is obtained from the flat morphism $U_0\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ by base change. Since flatness is preserved under base change, $\pi|_U$ is flat. Such neighborhoods $U$ cover $X$, so $\pi$ is flat.
